tour.overview:
The Great Barrier Reef stretches some 2,300 kilometres along the coast of Queensland, the largest coral reef system on Earth, with about 2,900 individual reefs and hundreds of islands. It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1981 and is home to some 1,500 species of fish, turtles, rays, sharks and giant clams. From Cairns, the outer reef, with the clearest water, is about 90 minutes by fast boat.

On this day you join a premium reef catamaran, with a private marine guide for your group who swims with you, finds the turtles and explains the reef. Private transfers to and from the marina are included.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 9 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in Cairns or Port Douglas
• Type: private transfers and private marine guide on a premium reef catamaran (shared vessel)
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy to moderate; swimming ability needed for snorkelling

WHAT YOU SEE
• Two outer reef sites.
• A glass-bottom boat or semi-submersible.
• A marine biologist talk.

WHY THIS WORKS
A private guide in the water makes snorkelling easier and safer for beginners and much richer for everyone.

WHO IT SUITS
Families, couples, snorkellers and divers.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
For a fully private reef experience, ask us about a private charter boat. For land and rainforest, choose our Daintree tour.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
Snorkelling equipment, wetsuits or stinger suits and buoyancy vests are provided. From November to May, stinger suits are worn as protection against jellyfish.

days.name: A catamaran to the outer reef, snorkelling with your guide, and lunch on board
days.description:
What to expect: a day on the outer reef with a private marine guide, snorkelling, a glass-bottom boat and lunch.

Your driver collects you at your hotel at about 7:15 and takes you to the Reef Fleet Terminal in Cairns, where you board a premium catamaran with your private marine guide. During the 90-minute crossing, a marine biologist explains the reef's ecology, and your guide fits your equipment.

At the first outer reef site, your guide leads you into the water and shows you the corals – brain, staghorn and plate corals – giant clams, parrotfish, clownfish in their anemones and, often, green sea turtles and reef sharks. If you wish, you can try an introductory dive with an instructor, no experience needed, or certified divers can dive. Lunch is served on board.

In the afternoon, you snorkel at a second site, and explore the reef from a glass-bottom boat or semi-submersible without getting wet. The catamaran returns to Cairns at about 16:30, and your driver takes you back to your hotel.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
07:15 – Pick-up at your hotel.
08:00 – Catamaran departs.
09:30 – First reef site: snorkelling.
12:00 – Lunch on board.
13:00 – Second reef site and glass-bottom boat.
15:00 – Return cruise.
16:30 – Arrival in Cairns and transfer.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Seasickness tablets are available on board; take them before departure if prone.
• Use reef-safe sun cream, or none, and a rash vest.
• A scenic helicopter return can be added.

INCLUDED: private transfers, private marine guide, catamaran, equipment, glass-bottom boat, lunch, reef tax.
NOT INCLUDED: dives, photos, drinks, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Is the boat private?
faq.answer: The catamaran is shared, but your guide and transfers are private. A fully private charter can be arranged at a higher price.

faq.question: Do we need to be good swimmers?
faq.answer: You need basic swimming ability. Buoyancy vests and your guide make snorkelling easy for beginners.

faq.question: Can we dive without experience?
faq.answer: Yes, an introductory dive with an instructor, after a short medical questionnaire.

faq.question: Are there jellyfish?
faq.answer: From November to May, stinger suits are provided and worn for protection.

faq.question: Is the reef still beautiful?
faq.answer: Yes. The outer reef sites we visit are among the healthiest, though coral bleaching affects parts of the reef.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Children from about 4 can snorkel with a vest; the glass-bottom boat suits everyone.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Partly. The catamaran has a main deck; getting into the water needs steps.

faq.question: What if the weather is bad?
faq.answer: If the operator cancels for weather, we rebook or refund you in full.

faq.question: What should we bring?
faq.answer: Swimwear, a towel, reef-safe sun cream, a hat and sunglasses.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: June to October has the calmest seas and best visibility; the reef can be visited all year.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tipping is not expected in Australia, where wages are higher, but it is always appreciated for excellent service.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 48 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
